Subject: Exploring a temporary seat->throughput swap for pilot
Attachments: Careloom_Metrics_Q3.pdf (pdf)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked great. We are preparing for a six-week pilot (starting late August) and have a practical packaging question: our usage is bursty — dashboarding teams will need steady low-latency inference for spikes, but the rest of the org doesn't use tokens constantly.

Is there a way to do a temporary exchange where we move N seats to guaranteed throughput for the pilot window (so we can keep features like streaming and function calling), then revert back to seats afterward? Also curious about how feature bundles (e.g., priority routing, KV cache retention, extended traces) are priced when attached to temporary throughput.

I attached our Q3 metrics and a short traffic sketch. If this works, I can loop in procurement for contract language.

Best,
Asha
Asha Verma

asha@careloom.io

Ben / Laura — looping you both in. Quick read: Careloom wants a six-week pilot, wants to convert some of their seats into guaranteed throughput for the pilot, and keep feature entitlements (streaming, function calls, KV cache). They prefer a time-bound amendment instead of a new SOW.

My thoughts:
- We can offer a temporary seat->throughput conversion by reserving a burst block for the pilot (explicit start/end dates).
- Pricing approaches: (1) prorated reserved throughput fee for the pilot window + a small reconfiguration fee; (2) keep seats but apply a temporary throughput overlay credit that guarantees X RPS; (3) hybrid — convert a subset of seats to throughput and provide a feature bundle add-on at a discounted rate.
- Feature bundles should be charged as add-ons pro rata. For short pilots I recommend a ~20-30% discount on add-ons if they commit to a follow-on dedicated capacity within 90 days.

Questions for Ben: what are minimum throughput blocks we can reserve in their region without breaking our density targets? Can we do an automated revert on the billing side (so seats come back online and entitlements return to normal)?

Asha — cc'd: we can sketch two concrete options and price them. Ben, Laura — can you draft a concise comparison table and a one-paragraph amendment template? Happy to run the concession through pricing.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kim / Laura / Asha —

Thanks for the context. Drafted two options (attached):

Option A — Temp Reserved Throughput
- Duration: 6 weeks (2026-08-24 to 2026-10-05)
- Reserved block: 150k tokens/day (~peak protection to cover spikes)
- Price: prorated reserved throughput fee = $9,000 (pro-rated monthly rate for block) + one-time reconfig fee $750
- Features: includes streaming, function calls, standard KV cache retention (30 days)
- Follow-on: if converted to Dedicated within 90 days, apply 25% credit on the reconfig fee and 20% on the first 3 months of committed throughput

Option B — Seat Overlay + Add-ons
- Keep current seats but apply an overlay guarantee of 70k tokens/day for pilot windows; cost = $5,000 prorated + add-on bundle $1,200 (20% pilot discount applied)
- No reconfig fee; quicker to enable.

Operational notes:
- Minimum throughput block in us-west is 100k tokens/day; we can split across two pools if needed.
- Billing can auto-revert — we tag the amendment with start/end dates and our billing engine will remove the overlay and restore seats after end_date. We'll confirm SLA language for the overlay guarantee.

Asha — if you like, I can turn Option A or B into a 1-page amendment and send to procurement for sign-off. Looking for a quick yes/no by Aug 10 to lock capacity.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
